name: Per Franzén
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Per Franzén joined publicly traded Swedish investment company EQT AB in 2007.
Franzen owns about 3% of EQT, which has roughly $83 billion (73,4 billion Euro) in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
Franzen's partners at EQT include billionaires Conni Johnson, Harry Klagsburn and Lennart Blecher, and Christian SInding.

name: Ibrahim Erdemoglu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Ibrahim Erdemoglu and his brother, Ali, together own over 75% of a top producer of materials used in carpet, SASA Polyester.
They initially acquired 51% of SASA in 2015 for $102 million, then added to their stake in the publicly traded company and watched it soar in value.
The brothers' Erdemoglu Holding also includes the two privately held companies, Merinos Carpet and Dinarsu Carpet.
In 1970, their father, Mehmet Erdemoglu, along with family members, started Merinos with two rug-weaving looms.
Today, Erdemoglu Holding is one of the world's largest carpet manufacturers, with production facilities in eight locations in Turkey and Russia.
forbes_facts: SASA has a $935 million licensing and technical service agreement with Invista, a subsidiary of Koch Industries that makes chemicals, polymers, fabrics and fibers.
While studying physics at university, Ibrahim Erdemoglu carried carpets on his back and sold them directly to customers.

name: Felipe Voigt Trejes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Felipe Voigt Trejes is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Felipe does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; his brother and younger sister are also major shareholders.

Tanaka is the company's chairman and CEO; he owns a substantial stake.

name: Martin Selig
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2016-2023); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Martin Selig is one of the biggest property developers in Seattle.
Selig owns more than 4 million square feet of office space in the city and has at least 1 million more under development.
Selig fled Nazi Germany with his family when he was age 3 and traveled through Poland, Russia and Korea until arriving by boat in Seattle.
Selig started working at his father's linen store in Seattle when he was eleven years old.
He started his real estate business in 1958 by building shopping malls.
forbes_facts: One of his daughters is a film producer.
Selig is a painter and an art collector; he enjoys bicycling, riding his Harley motorcycle and skiing.

name: Christian Bertermann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Hurun Global U40 (2021); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Christian Bertermann and Hakan Koç cofounded Auto1 and grew the used car marketplace to become one of Europe's most valuable startups.
Auto1 went public on the Frankfurt stock exchange in February 2021; Bertermann is the CEO.
Bertermann worked at a German Groupon-like company and then Groupon after the American deals marketplace snapped up its German rival.
He met his cofounder Hakan Koç while they worked in the same building at different startups in Berlin.
The pair were inspired to found the business after Bertermann struggled to sell his grandmother's Mercedes and a VW Golf.
